schemaNote: 効果音ラボ (Sound Effect Lab) SFX pack — real recorded material, staged by task #51. Sibling of sfx/fx/ (synthesised) but THIRD-PARTY licensed: read `licence` before touching, moving or re-exporting anything here.
reason: sfx/fx/ is 21 synthesised lavfi clips: correct physics, no material. Every weapon in GGD sounds like the same band-passed noise whoosh regardless of blade, bow or gun, and whole classes of event (shop denial, gold, panel open/close, low health, explosion, heal, buff, elemental abilities, match end) had NO sound bound at all. These are real recordings that fill exactly those gaps.

licence.source: 効果音ラボ (Sound Effect Lab) — https://soundeffect-lab.info/
licence.criticalSourceWarning: Byte-identical copies of many of these clips are also published on ニコニ・コモンズ under a DIFFERENT, commercial-RESTRICTED licence. Only the soundeffect-lab.info copy carries the free-commercial terms recorded here. Never re-acquire these files from ニコニ・コモンズ or any mirror; if a clip must be replaced, re-download it from the sourcePage recorded on that clip.
licence.commercialUse: PERMITTED, unconditionally and free of charge — 「個人、法人、公的機関問わず無料で使用可能（商用利用無料）」. Paid vs free product makes no difference (「有料か無料かに関係なく、料金発生なし、報告不要、クレジット表記不要」); overseas commercial use is explicitly fine.
licence.attribution: NOT REQUIRED — optional (「使用にあたっての報告、リンク、クレジット表記不要（禁止ではなく任意）」). Belongs in the COURTESY bucket of content/assets/CREDITS.md, NOT the MANDATORY bucket with the 魔王魂 BGM and the CC-BY 4.0 dragon.
licence.copyright: NOT waived. Copyright is retained by 効果音ラボ (「素材の著作権は放棄していないため」); the voice actors assigned all rights except 著作者人格権 by contract. This is a PERMISSIVE LICENCE, NOT CC0 / public domain — do not merge these rows into the CC0 block of CREDITS.md.

creditWording.note: The site specifies these exact strings (「効果音ラボと表記いただければ問題ございません」/「Sound Effect Lab とさせていただいております」). Use them verbatim if we credit.

licence.formatConversionAllowed: YES — 「WAVやOGGなどどのような形式に変換していただいても構いません」, so the WAV/MP3 + mono/44.1 kHz + normalisation pipeline below is explicitly sanctioned.
licence.shippingRawFilesAllowed: YES — shipping a game/app with the audio files exposed, including publishing it on GitHub, is explicitly NOT redistribution (「音源ファイルむき出しで配布・販売して良いですか？」→「問題ございません」). The site asks, as a courtesy only, that we obscure the files where technically convenient (「できる限りでよいので…技術的に難しければしなくても構いません」).
prohibitions: 再配布 (redistribution) of the raw files. Also covers 「効果音が重要な役割を果たすコンテンツ」. GGD is safe: 「アプリに操作音として効果音を組み込む」 is listed under 再配布ではないケース.

CONCRETE GGD RULE — the asset editor must NOT ship a soundboard / sound-test screen or any admin feature that lets a user freely audition and download this pack clip by clip. That is the one build we could plausibly make that WOULD trip 再配布.
Redistributing MODIFIED versions. Editing for use INSIDE the game (trim, normalise, WAV conversion, layering) is fine; publishing an edited file as a standalone asset is not.
AI TRAINING is forbidden (「AI学習用のデータとして利用することは禁止」). We CANNOT feed these voice clips to a TTS/voice-clone model to synthesise bespoke lines in the same actress's voice. That path is closed.

Any use of the 声素材 that harms the voice actors (「声優の尊厳を傷つけたり、声優が被害を被る使い方は禁止」). GGD RULE: play their lines WHOLE. Never re-cut an actress's syllables into a new insulting sentence she did not record — in particular do not splice these into the mocking 白目 taunt register.
Hotlinking (直リンク). Files are self-hosted here; the client must NEVER fetch soundeffect-lab.info at runtime.
Anything that restricts other people's use of the same SFX: no YouTube Content ID registration of material containing them, no 音商標 (sound trademark) registration of a GGD jingle built from them.
Making a video that showcases/introduces the sound effects. A normal gameplay trailer is fine; an 'audio pass devlog' that plays the clips one by one to demo them is not.

pipeline.target: mono, 44.1 kHz — mono so WebAudio can spatialise, 44.1 kHz to match sfx/fx/ and the rest of the tree.
pipeline.wavVsMp3: 16-bit PCM WAV for short transient-led clips (the attack carries the information; MP3 encoder delay/padding is applied inconsistently by browser decodeAudioData and would shift a 40 ms attack). libmp3lame 192 kbps CBR mono for the longer tonal/ambient beds and for all voice, where a few ms of leading padding is inaudible and the size saving is real. Boundary used: transient-led AND <= ~2.0 s post-trim -> WAV, else MP3.
pipeline.trim: silenceremove at -55 dB peak on both ends (via areverse), retaining 20 ms of pad, so a soft attack is never clipped.
pipeline.declick: Clips whose signal still exceeds -35 dB at the final 25 ms get a 20 ms fade-out, so the buffer does not end on a non-zero sample and click. Applied to exactly 4 clips (see per-clip `processing`). bow-draw.mp3 is the important one: 弓を引き絞る1 is a sustained creak that the SOURCE cuts off mid-signal.
pipeline.sfxNormalisation: peak-normalised to -3.0 dBFS, exactly like sfx/fx/*.wav. Relative loudness between events is set by `gain` in content/config/audio-map.json, NEVER by re-rendering the file.
pipeline.voiceNormalisation: mean -15.0 dB with a -1.5 dB peak ceiling — the same targetMeanDb/peakCeilingDb the announcer generator (tools/tts-gen) applies, so these land in the announcer band (-15.0..-18.2 dB mean) and can sit in the same pools without a level seam.
pipeline.clippingNote: magic-fire.mp3's source peaks at 0.0 dBFS and its mono downmix overshoots full scale, so the first gain estimate read back off a clamped 16-bit stage file. The builder re-measures and corrects (final gain -5.6 dB, not the -3.0 a single pass would have produced). Every peak below is verified, not assumed.
pipeline.sampleRateNote: The voice clips are kept at 44.1 kHz even though announcer/*.mp3 and voices/names/*.mp3 are 22.05 kHz. Those two packs are Apple-`say` MACHINE TTS placeholders whose 22.05 kHz is an artefact of the generator; these are real 44.1 kHz recordings and downsampling to 'match' a placeholder would be a pure quality loss.

bindingNote: PARTIALLY WIRED as of the #51 ledger phase, once task #40 had LANDED (announcer pools are announcer/-only and announcer.ja-JP.json is in place). `ggdEvent` on each clip remains the INTENDED binding and `suggestedGain` an equal-loudness starting point computed as anchorGain * 10^((anchorMeanDb - thisMeanDb)/20) against the clip named in `gainAnchor` — a starting value for a human ear, not a measured result. Events written `abilityCast:fire` are per-ability overrides, not new top-level events. What ACTUALLY landed in content/config/audio-map.json is recorded in `bindings` below; the per-clip `ggdEvent` was NOT rewritten, so where the two disagree `bindings` is the authority.

bindings.route: Surgical additive edit to content/config/audio-map.json. Two existing pools were replaced with real recordings; sixteen NEW event keys were authored. Nothing else in the file was touched, and no announcer/system pool was touched at all.

bindings.forbiddenBindings: matchStart, levelUp and exUnlock are ANNOUNCER-VO-ONLY pools. Task #40 made every system broadcast Japanese and packages/shared/src/content/announcerVo.test.ts asserts those pools contain nothing outside assets/audio/announcer/. That is why the gong, the jingle and the holy sting got their OWN keys (matchStartGong / levelUpJingle / exUnlockSting) — they are meant to be LAYERED ALONGSIDE the VO, never mixed into its pool. Do not 'simplify' them back.
bindings.deliberatelyUnbound: Every weapon clip (attack-sword-1/2, attack-greatsword, attack-katana, bow-draw, arrow-release, arrow-pierce, gunshot, impact-heavy), cast-circle, and the three elemental casts (magic-fire, magic-ice, magic-lightning). basicAttack / projectileSpawn / projectileHit / attackWindup / abilityCast are single GLOBAL events — GGD has no per-weapon or per-ability audio routing — so a katana slash bound there lands on a mage's staff and a fletched arrow on a fireball. Secondary blockers recorded per clip in the CREDITS.md ledger: attack-katana is +7.4 dB vs the pool anchor, attack-greatsword is 1.70 s against a 90 ms cooldown, cast-circle is 3.50 s against castBegin's 120 ms cooldown, and impact-heavy would fight fx/crit.mp3's rising-sting legibility. These clips are the raw material for per-weapon routing (client-audio work), not a drop-in upgrade.
bindings.ledger: content/assets/CREDITS.md — section '効果音ラボ / Sound Effect Lab pack'. Summary + pipeline + regeneration story in content/assets/audio/README.md.

phase2.note: SECOND audio-coverage wave. This section is a LEDGER only; it is NOT the `clips` array (ACQUIRE.py iterates `clips` and would fail on any entry without a soundeffect-lab.info sourceUrl/sourceBytes). Two groups: (A) nine NEW event clips downloaded THIS run into lab/, and (B) the per-weapon / per-element clips that were on disk and `deliberatelyUnbound` above, now given their OWN dedicated routing keys so the combat emit agent can address them individually. audio-map.json is the authority for the exact gain/cooldown/maxConcurrent that landed; sfxManifest.ts is the authority for preload + loop flagging.
phase2.licence: courtesy — same permissive, attribution-OPTIONAL bucket as the rest of this pack (see `licence` above). No mandatory-attribution change: the CC-BY login dragon stays the one mandatory in-game credit. Recorded in CREDITS.md's COURTESY bucket, not the CC0 block and not the mandatory block.

perWeaponRouting.note: Group B — SUPERSEDES the `bindings.deliberatelyUnbound` note FOR THESE CLIPS ONLY. They were unbound because GGD had a single GLOBAL basicAttack/projectileSpawn/abilityCast event; the combat emit agent (next phase) is adding per-weapon / per-element routing, so each clip now gets its OWN top-level key in audio-map.json to route to. gain = the clip's suggestedGain from `clips`; cooldown/maxConcurrent mirror the clip's original anchor event. They stay OUT of the `clips` array for the same reason as Group A: ACQUIRE.py additionally requires sourceBytes + pre/post dB, which this acquisition did not capture. VERIFY.py still gates their on-disk format because it globs the tree, not this ledger.

Searched 演出・アニメ plus the site search for ファンファーレ / 当たり / 当選 / 獲得; the only non-voice fanfares were trumpet1.mp3 and levelup1.mp3, and levelup1 is already in the pack as level-up-jingle.mp3, so trumpet1 is the distinct jackpot flourish. The literal 「大当たり～」 hits were 声素材 voice clips (info-girl1-ooatari1.mp3) — deliberately NOT used: a spoken Japanese line would clash with the gacha reveal and falls under the pack's voice-actor restrictions. MPEG ADTS layer III v1, 192 kbps, 44.1 kHz JntStereo, 1.888 s; raw mean -23.5 dB, max -6.9 dB. suggestedGain 1.44 is an ESTIMATE assuming the standard peak-normalise to -3.0 dBFS, computed against gainAnchor level-up-jingle.mp3 (post mean -17.8 dB @ 1.17) — re-measure after processing. Given the vsReveal / matchEndGong stinger treatment: long cooldown, single voice.

clips.note: THE CASTER'S BASIC ATTACK. Acquired 2026-07-24 because there was no clip for one: sim/systems/BasicAttackSystem.weaponClassOf had no caster weapon class, so all 21 conjuring champions fell to the ranged default and answered a spell with bow-draw.mp3. Picked over magic-flame1/magic-ice1/magic-electron2 (already bound as the abilityCast element whooshes — reusing one would conflate the auto with the spell) and over magic-stick1 (3.4 s sparkle wash, no transient: unusable on a ~1.5 s attack cadence). 気弾1 is a short anime energy-bolt with a hard onset, the shared abstraction over every missile art in the roster.
clips.processing: decode mp3 -> aresample 44100 -> downmix mono -> trim edge silence (silenceremove peak -55 dB, 20 ms pad both ends) -> volume -0.40 dB -> libmp3lame 128 kbps mono (the #158 ceiling, matching every other shipped lab clip — ACQUIRE.py's literal 192k predates it)
